intro: Professionals and everyday users convert metric tons (t) to imperial long tons (ton (UK)) when working across metric and imperial standards in engineering specifications, international trade documentation, and technical measurements. One metric ton (tonne / megagram) equals 0.984207 imperial long tons, while 1 imperial long ton equals 1.016047 metric tons. Whether you are verifying mass & weight specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Short Ton (US) vs. Metric Tonne (t) vs. Long Ton (UK)
items: Three distinct units are called a "ton": the US Short Ton equals 2,000 lbs (907.185 kg), the Metric Tonne (t) equals 1,000 kg (2,204.62 lbs), and the British Imperial Long Ton equals 2,240 lbs (1,016.05 kg).
Confusing US short tons with metric tonnes introduces a 10.2% freight weight error on international bills of lading.

faqs.question: How many imperial long tons (ton (UK)) are in 1 metric ton (tonne / megagram) (t)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.98420653 imperial long tons (ton (UK)) in 1 metric ton (tonne / megagram) (t), which rounds to 0.9842 ton (UK) for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 imperial long ton equals 1.016047 metric tons.

faqs.question: How do I convert metric tons to imperial long tons (t to ton (UK))?
faqs.answer: To convert metric tons to imperial long tons, use the formula: ton (UK) = t × 0.98420653. For example, converting 10 t gives 9.8421 ton (UK).

faqs.question: What is 10 metric tons in imperial long tons?
faqs.answer: 10 metric tons (t) equals exactly 9.8421 imperial long tons (ton (UK)) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
